claim: Let \(G\) be a finite connected simple graph, let \(g\in V(G)\), and let \(\sigma_g(G)=\{\theta:E_\theta e_g\ne0\}\) be the adjacency eigenvalue support of \(g\). For \(d\ge2\), let \(a,b\) be antipodal vertices of the \(d\)-cube \(Q_d\), and use the standard adjacency Hamiltonian on the lexicographic product \(G[Q_d]\), whose adjacency matrix is \(A_G\otimes J_{2^d}+I\otimes A_{Q_d}\). Then perfect state transfer from \((g,a)\) to \((g,b)\) occurs if and only if \(\sigma_g(G)\subseteq\mathbb Z\). When it occurs, the complete set of positive transfer times is \(t=(2r+1)\pi/2\), \(r=0,1,2,\ldots\); in particular the minimum time is \(\pi/2\). More precisely, at an arbitrary time \(t\), such transfer is possible only if \(\cos t=0\) and \(e^{-i2^d tA_G}e_g=e_g\). This strictly strengthens the earlier sufficient condition requiring all of \(G\) to be integral. For example, let \(T\) be the seven-vertex tree with a degree-two vertex \(g\) joining two degree-three vertices, each of which has two pendant leaves. Then \(\phi_T(x)=x^3(x^2-2)(x^2-4)\), so \(T\) is nonintegral, while \(\phi_{T-g}(x)=x^2(x^2-2)^2\) and the local support at \(g\) is exactly \(\{-2,0,2\}\). Hence \(T[Q_d]\) is a connected nonintegral graph with perfect state transfer between the two antipodes in the \(g\)-fiber at time \(\pi/2\) for every \(d\ge2\).

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the theorem; exact polynomial and finite numerical checks are supplementary
integrity.novelty_scope: Necessary-and-sufficient vertex-local integrality criterion, exact transfer-time set, and a connected nonintegral outer-graph example beyond the published global-integrality corollary.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The lexicographic-product decomposition and global sufficient condition are credited to Ge et al.; general eigenvalue-support theory is credited to Godsil; later blow-up support theory is credited separately.

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the standard adjacency Hamiltonian and antipodes within one hypercube fiber.
The hypercube dimension is at least two; the one-dimensional case has a different parity condition.
Transfer between different outer fibers, generalized lexicographic products, Laplacian walks, and pretty-good transfer are not classified.
The result is a local sharpening of known lexicographic-product spectral machinery, so an equivalent corollary may exist under periodic-vertex terminology.
title: Vertex-local integrality exactly characterizes hypercube-fiber transfer in lexicographic products
